newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up against dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up against dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed higher on Friday at 8.2889 against the dollar from Thursday's 8.2893 after China showed a large trade surplus and the central bank governor said the currency was under pressure to rise.
Beijing announced on Thursday that the trade surplus had hit $20.53 billion in the first seven months of this year, up from $1.965 billion in the same 1996 period.
"The large trade surplus had been expected by the market, but it still helped to push the yuan up," one trader said.
Dealers said comments by Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China, on Thursday also supported the yuan.
Dai said the yuan was under pressure to rise after foreign exchange reserves hit $126 billion at the end of July.
"The market sees the remarks as positive for the yuan's upward trend with the central government saying the yuan is under pressure to rise," a second trader said.
Active buying had helped to push the yuan far above the key level of 8.2900, another dealer said.
However, trading was dull before the weekend with dealers usually conducting less business on Fridays, traders said.
Dealers said the yuan still had potential to rise further next week but no sharp increases were expected.
The yuan opened sharply lower at an intraday low of 8.2948 on one speculative deal and recovered quickly to move around the 8.2890 level for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2887.
The weighted average rate on Thursday was 8.2893.
The yuan closed up at 7.0350 from 7.1481 against 100 Japanese yen and up slightly at 1.0698 from 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar.
